translation_notes: RDF.type -> rdf:type and SH.ValidationResult -> sh:ValidationResult inside the report.triples((None, ..., ...)) pattern; that is the region's entire translatable surface
the draft placed the two @prefix statements between the imports and the first string constant; moved above the imports, right after the header comments
original.py runs as extracted (pyshacl is installed in the evaluation venv); no shim needed

finding: the two big Turtle documents (the SHACL shapes and the data) are Python *string constants* parsed at run time -- precisely the pattern g{} exists to replace, and the biggest available notation win in this example. Inlining them would restructure parse-into-graph as construct-a-graph, which the faithfulness rule forbids, so they stay strings and the win is left on the table. Two of them would also resist a naive move: sh:message contains '{?Class2Instance}', which g{} would read as an interpolation, and sh:select holds a triple-quoted SPARQL query

finding: run_pair can only compare the return value (None) and the arguments (none), so equivalence rests on the region's own assertion, len(result_list) == 2, holding on both sides -- a real check (a mis-resolved sh:ValidationResult yields an empty list and an AssertionError), but a narrower one than a graph comparison
